name: ElasticSlider-TS-TW

frames.best_why: The track is stretched past its right end and the speaker icon enlarged, the one frame that shows the elastic stretch.

tagline: A volume bar stretches past its end and snaps back.
summary: A flat grey slider sets a value shown above it, with a muted speaker on the left and a loud one on the right. Dragging beyond an end stretches the track and grows that icon until it springs back.
appearance: Inside a dark rounded card, a thin grey track runs between a muted speaker icon and a louder one, its filled part a slightly darker grey. A small number sits centred above the bar, under a 'Volume' title and a line of helper text.
behaviour: Dragging the bar moves the filled portion and updates the number above. Pulling past either end stretches the track outward and enlarges the end icon, both springing back on release.
demo_content: Card heading 'Volume', helper line 'Pull past either end to feel the stretch.', and values between 0 and 100.
search_phrases: volume bar that stretches when pulled
range input that bounces at the ends
volume setting inside a settings card
use_when: A volume or intensity control should feel playful and show its limits with a physical stretch.
avoid_when: The track only responds to pointer drags and has no keyboard or screen-reader support.
customise: Starting value, default value, maximum, step size, stepped mode and the two end icons are props; the surrounding card is demo markup.
weight_why: One motion value drives a single track transform, springing only while dragged.

a11y.note: The bar is a plain div with pointer handlers: no role, no tab stop and no value announcement, so it cannot be used without a mouse.

issues: The helper line and value label are faint grey on the dark card, low enough to be hard to read.
polish_why: The stretch and snap is a nice touch and the card is tidy, though the track styling is plain grey.
